I'm 63 this year, and I've been farming these 9 mu in Quzhou for 45 years — started when I was 18. My husband and I are the only ones left at home now; our children work in Shijiazhuang. With just the two of us and our ages, labor is my biggest worry every year. I finished senior high school, so unlike some neighbors, I can read the extension bulletins and work out fertilizer rates from the soil condition. But honestly, after four and a half decades, I mostly trust my eyes — the wheat color, the soil texture, how the cotton bolls set.

I divide the 9 mu into two blocks: 7 mu for wheat-maize double cropping, which is our bread and butter, and 2 mu for cotton. I've thought about dropping cotton — it's heavy on labor with all the picking — but that 2 mu gives us about 500 kg of seed cotton each year, and the cash comes right when we need it for the next season's inputs. Besides, I've grown cotton for 30 years; I know its temperament.

The wheat in the ground now — I planted Jinmai 47 last October 12th, right after the National Day rains. It's a good semi-dwarf variety, doesn't lodge easily. I applied 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, plus 15 kg urea as base. In mid-March, when the wheat was at regreening, I topdressed another 12 kg urea per mu because the leaves looked a bit light. Now it's late April, the wheat is at jointing-heading. I'm watching it closely — if the color stays light after this week's warm spell, I'll do one more light topdress of 8 kg urea per mu before heading. I'll irrigate twice more: once at heading in early May, once at grain filling in late May. Pumping costs me about 45 yuan per irrigation for the 7 mu, so that's 90 yuan more, but without it I'd lose 50 kg per mu easy. I'm hoping for 480-500 kg/mu this year if no late frost hits the heads.

For cotton, I'll plant in the next 3-4 days — around April 25th. I use a local mid-season variety, not the expensive hybrids. I save my own seed when the quality is good, which saves about 30 yuan per mu. This year I'm using saved seed from 2024 — last year's seed looked strong. I'll rotary till the 2 mu and put down 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting. At flowering in July, I'll topdress with 10 kg urea per mu. Cotton needs water at flowering and boll-setting, so two irrigations, maybe three if July is scorching. The bollworm is the enemy — I'll spray insecticide twice, and use herbicide once. The real cost is picking. My back won't let me bend all day anymore, so I hire 2-3 women from the village for about 10 days total at 80 yuan per day. That's 800 yuan, but there's no choice at our age.

Summer maize goes in immediately after wheat harvest — June 15th to 18th, that narrow window. I'll hire the tractor with the straw chopper and no-till planter; there's no time for plowing between crops. Zhengdan 958, the hybrid — everyone uses it, 45 yuan per mu for seed. I'll apply 45 kg compound fertilizer plus 10 kg urea per mu at planting, all at once because there's no time to come back. If rains are good, I'll irrigate twice: right after planting if the soil is dry, and at the big trumpet stage in late July. That trumpet-stage irrigation is critical — miss it and you lose 100 kg per mu. One spray for corn borer, one herbicide application. I expect 520-550 kg/mu if the summer rains are normal.

Total costs this year: seeds about 500 yuan, fertilizers around 2400 yuan, irrigation pumping 600 yuan, pesticides 500 yuan, hired labor for cotton picking and harvest help 1300 yuan, machine services for planting and combining 700 yuan. About 6000 yuan total. That's a big chunk of our savings, but last year's wheat price was decent so we have enough cash. Still, I'm not increasing fertilizer beyond what I planned — at our age, we can't afford a bad year.

My biggest concern is that week between wheat harvest and maize planting. If the combine breaks down or it rains, the whole schedule shifts. And if my husband's knee flares up again, I'll need even more hired help. That's why I keep some cash in reserve — I won't push the N rate to 22 kg per mu even though the extension office says it could get me 550 kg. I'd rather be a bit safe and have money for emergencies.
